title: Research
text:
PhD thesis
Beyond Human Interaction: Alternative Applications for Explanations (TU Berlin / DFKI, since 2023)
Exploring how model explanations can be useful beyond helping people interpret predictions. Current work uses methods such as Integrated Gradients, ALTI, LRP, and residual-stream analysis to detect distribution shifts, improve document retrieval, and identify hallucinations.

title: Research
text:
Current research
Hallucination detection: Checking whether generated answers are supported by retrieved sources.
Document retrieval: Using attribution methods to explain embedding similarity and improve ranking.
Distribution shift detection: Detecting changes in input data through model explanations, without labelled examples.
Controlled generation: Controlling text length in diffusion language models.

title: Projects
text:
Training-Free Character-Length Control in Summarization with Diffusion Language Models, EMNLP 2026 (main conference)
DELTA controls the character length of summaries generated by masked diffusion language models without fine-tuning. It adjusts masked positions during generation and reduces length errors by roughly an order of magnitude across three benchmarks, while maintaining summary quality. Developed within GenKI4Media for applications such as headlines and previews.

title: Projects
text:
Hallucination detection from model internals
Research within GenKI4Media on detecting whether generated answers are supported by retrieved documents. The approach examines contributions from source text and previously generated tokens in the residual stream, using these signals for training-free and supervised detection.
An extended abstract appeared at BlackboxNLP 2026. A full paper is forthcoming. A related poster was presented at the AI Grid Summer School in Paris.

title: Projects
text:
GUARDRAIL
Grounded Uncertainty-Aware Reasoning with Deferrable, Reliable Abstention In LLMs
A Franco-German AI for Science 2026 proposal on making LLM-generated knowledge graphs more reliable. Source evidence and uncertainty are retained with extracted facts and used for retrieval, climate-related claim verification (ClimateCheck), and deciding when the system should abstain. The work also considers plant- and pest-related question answering.
Partners: DFKI Berlin, University of Bamberg (Cognitive Systems), Lamarr Institute / University of Bonn, Université Paris-Saclay, and INRAE MaIAGE. Developed at the AI for Science Summer School (AI Grid, DataIA, SCAI), coordinated from DFKI Berlin.

title: Projects
text:
NEXUS
Knowledge-Driven and Interpretable Reranking for Scientific Document Retrieval (Neuro-symbolic EXplainable Scientific Search)
A Franco-German AI for Science 2026 proposal on improving scientific search with domain ontologies. Documents and queries are linked to ontology concepts, aligned across ontologies with expert-checked LLM suggestions, and compared through late-interaction reranking. This also shows which concepts explain the ranking, evaluated on biomedical literature.
Partners: DFKI Berlin, TIB Hannover, Friedrich Schiller University Jena, and Université de Technologie de Compiègne (BMBI Laboratory). Developed at the AI for Science Summer School (AI Grid, DataIA, SCAI). The DFKI contribution covers concept representations, reranking, and explanation evaluation.

Generative AI assistants for the media, cultural and creative sectors (BMFTR, 2025 to present)
Developing more reliable AI tools for editorial work by checking generated content against external sources. The DFKI work focuses on hallucination detection and precise text-length control.
Partners: 3pc, ART+COM, Fraunhofer FOKUS, dpa, and Deutsche Welle.
